weeks.recapTitle: Some Guys Have All the Luck
weeks.bestPlay: Dania building on Hussein's port and knocking him out of the game early.
weeks.summary: We're going to keep this short and sweet. Hassan got attacked. Abe got longest road and then got attacked. Ali didn't get attacked-and won.

weeks.recapTitle: Abe and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day
weeks.bestPlay: Ali for the resource monopoly heard about the world.
weeks.worstPlay: Rasha for not using the inventor on Ali’s spot even though he was about to win.
weeks.summary:
Sometimes prayers go unanswered and people lose faith. This week, the last ray of hope was taken from the settlers as Ali ran roughshod over the rest with a dominating—and for some, humiliating—loss. Sheik Hussein was heard wondering whether he’d be better off worshiping a different deity next week after his last-place finish this week.

There’s not much to be said about this bloodbath. The turning point in the game came when Abe spent about 15 minutes scratching his head, trying to make 3 for 1 deals, making us all wonder what he was up to. All of that ended up with him turning in his hand for three ore. The settlers waited for his next move and in amazement, he said, “It’s time for free play,” with the three ore in his hand. The very next turn, Ali used Resource Monopoly on ore and stole five ore from the settlers, including two Abe had worked tirelessly for. In a savage play, Ali also took two ore from Hassan just after he had finally gathered enough for a city. Abe simmered and stewed for the rest of the game, trying to seek revenge, but at that point it was a fait accompli.

Rasha had her third moral victory in a row, beating High Priest Hussein from the Satanic Society in Garden City.

Well, at least soon-to-be Dr. Lena showed up and played a respectable game.

Hassan played this game just to make sure everyone knew Dania was still the reigning champion. Since she didn’t play this week, he spared himself from another night sleeping on the ground.

weeks.bestPlay: Ali for stealing Hassan's coin metropolis in one turn and costing Hassan the game.
weeks.worstPlay: Hassan and Rasha for giving Dania the wool metropolis without a fight.
weeks.summary:
Catan is a battle. And sometimes that battle becomes a war.

This week's matchup was all-out war because Hussein, with the bravado of Napoleon Dynamite and the bite of a chihuahua, declared his prolonged losing streak would end tonight.

Like World War II, there were heroes. This week's hero, to the surprise of many, was Dania.

Dania is an inspiration to every young mother. Just six weeks postpartum, she returned from maternity leave with her baby on her lap and a bottle in her hand. She shocked us all by getting a win before the hosts.

In World War II, we had Rosie the Riveter. In the war declared by Hussein, we have Dania the Humble. She was the most unassuming champion, and she spent the evening thanking each of us individually for her victory in a way that felt anything but humble.

In war, there are winners and losers, and there were two big losers this evening. First was Ali, whose game sputtered from the start. He had an ideal opening strategy, which Hussein promptly jinxed by asking everyone to start over the moment Ali placed his starting spots. However, the biggest loser of the night was Abe. Abe went from worst to first and spent the rest of the evening exasperated because nothing he tried worked. By the end, both of them were basically just rolling dice and waiting for suhoor.

Morale victories do not mean much in wars, but for Rasha, that was as good as it gets right now. It was another close call, and she also tied for worst play of the week with Hassan.

In wars, you have to execute. Hassan had a great battle plan, had the spots, had the rolls, and still could not finish. The best play of the day came when Ali stole Hassan's metropolis with nine coins in a single turn, right before Hassan was about to win the game. The worst play of the day was the lack of urgency from both Rasha and Hassan around the wool metropolis. Hassan practically had it in his hands if he had played it right. Rasha seemed determined to hand Dania the metropolis for the win instead of taking it herself by trading her wool. In war, sometimes the smartest tactic is simple defense, and they could not execute it or prolong the game. They let Dania take the wool metropolis and seal the victory.

Lena sat out again, maybe scared off by the war-themed evening. Rola declared herself anti-violence and decided to stay home.

weeks.recapTitle: Abe's Trifecta: Best Play, Worst Play and the Win
weeks.bestPlay: Abe getting three points on his final turn to steal the win by breaking Hussein's longest road. It is hard to win when you have the worst play and the best play in the same week, but he is an enimga.
weeks.worstPlay: Abe used his spy to steal an irrigation card and gleefully played it without realizing the bank had no wheat left.
weeks.summary:
Abe finally got on the board with a midnight heist--snatching Longest Road and dropping three points in a single turn. A rare burst of decisiveness from the guy who usually thinks for five minutes and then accomplishes nothing.

Ali stuck to his usual strategy: tell everyone he has no chance of winning, then somehow end up right there again--until a dry spell and a badly timed 7 cost him the win.

Rasha showed up after months of just rolling dice and, in the second most surprising thing of the night, nearly won. We're counting that as a win for her.

Hassan had flashes of brilliance but, as usual, couldn't close. Second-worst play of the night: helping Ali save his city while Hussein and Rasha were about to explode.

And instead of Rasha rolling dice all night, Hussein took over as the designated roller--trash-talking loudly while extending his streak: another week without a win.

Lena stayed home, shocked that Abe went to game night while she was sick instead of taking care of her. Dania spent the night changing diapers while plotting how to make it next week.

We're still waiting on Rola to make her first appearance.
